children: The National Stock Exchange has not applied to the Securities and Exchange Board of India for permission to trade its own shares on its platform, managing director and CEO Ashishkumar Chauhan said on September 11, days before the exchange’s much-awaited initial public offering.

The clarification comes as NSE prepares to open its ₹11,000-crore IPO for subscription on September 17. The issue will close on September 21, with anchor investor bidding scheduled for September 16. The shares are expected to list on September 24.
NSE has set a price band of ₹1,700 to ₹1,785 a share for the IPO.

Chauhan’s comments come amid reports that NSE shares could potentially trade in the “permitted to trade” category on the exchange even though the formal listing would take place on the BSE. Bloomberg reported last month, citing people familiar with the matter, that such a route was being considered.
Speaking at a press conference in Mumbai, Chauhan highlighted the scale and evolution of NSE.

“NSE is India’s largest exchange and by many counts, it’s one of the largest in the world. The purpose of NSE was also to channel savings into capital. It’s a testament that NSE has fulfilled the mandate its founders started with,” he said.
Chauhan also highlighted NSE’s technology capabilities and its presence across asset classes.

“We are among the largest vertically integrated exchanges in the sense that we own our technology. Some exchanges focus on commodities or equities. We are across asset classes, commodities, currencies, electricity, even charity,” he said.
On technology, Chauhan said NSE has built its systems around continuous availability, with response times of 500–800 nanoseconds.
NSE profit falls as options trading drives revenue
NSE reported a profit of ₹10,300 crore for the financial year ended March 2026, down 15% from a year earlier.
Revenue, however, more than doubled between April 2019 and March 2026 to about ₹18,700 crore, helped by a sharp increase in options trading.

NSE has about 95% of India's cash equity market and around 75% of the equity derivatives market, according to its disclosures. It is also the world’s largest derivatives exchange by contracts traded and accounted for roughly 89% of global stock index options volumes in 2025, according to data from the World Federation of Exchanges.
Investors turn bullish on NSE IPO
Market participants expect the IPO to receive a strong response.
Harsha Raghavan, managing partner at Convergent Finance, told CNBC-TV18 that he sees “tremendous volume growth” ahead for NSE as India's wealth increases.

He described NSE as a “top down play” and one of the best ways to participate in the financialisation of India. Raghavan expects the stock to deliver a 20–25% return in the first six weeks after listing, while also pointing to improving performance among small- and mid-cap stocks and a broader wave of corporate buybacks.
Ramesh Damani, a member of the BSE, said NSE has taken Indian markets “out of the stone ages” through the digitalisation and democratisation of trading.

Damani expects the IPO to be “a very well received issue” and believes NSE can continue to be a growth stock. He said investors should look beyond the headline indices, where opportunities remain across overlooked stocks despite strong underlying market performance.

With the IPO just days away, NSE’s dominant market position, technology infrastructure and the continued financialisation of Indian savings are likely to remain central to the investment case as the exchange prepares to enter the public markets.

title: NSE IPO: CEO says exchange has not sought SEBI permission to trade its shares on its own platform
